observation.visible_scene: An indoor room shot at floor level: a closed white paneled door on the left, a plain beige wall, a concrete floor, and a wall electrical box with a bent metal conduit and a red wire running along the baseboard. At the far left edge a person's dark shoe and lower leg are partially visible. A single pink ball sits on the floor in front of the door.
visible_changes: In the first two frames the pink ball rests on the floor at roughly the same spot.

From frame 3 onward the ball lifts off the floor and moves steadily upward in a near-vertical line, its horizontal position staying essentially fixed (~left-of-center) while its height in the frame increases continuously.
By the last frame the ball has risen to about mid-door height, well above the floor and the red wire.
The door, wall, outlet, conduit, red wire, and the person's shoe at the left edge do not change position across the segment, indicating the camera is static and the background is fixed.
The ball's apparent size stays roughly constant, consistent with vertical motion in the image plane rather than strong motion toward or away from the camera.
outside_clip_unknowns: What caused the ball to leave the floor (a bounce, a toss, or another contact) is not shown within the excerpt.
Whether the ball is at the start of an ascent or the tail of a bounce, and what happens after the last frame (descent, contact, or stop), is not visible.
uncertain_details: The exact nature of the upward motion (rising after an unseen bounce vs. a thrown arc's ascending portion) cannot be determined from the frames alone.
No object or person is seen touching the ball during the segment; the left-edge foot remains stationary throughout.
